title: Describing things
goal: Describe people and things by colour, size, age and quality, and compare them (bigger, the biggest).
intro:
Many Nepali adjectives end in **-ओ** — रातो 'red', ठूलो 'big', राम्रो 'good' — and these change their ending to agree with the noun: राम्रो केटा 'a nice boy', राम्री केटी 'a nice girl', राम्रा मान्छेहरू 'nice people'. Adjectives ending in anything else never change.

Comparison is easy: Nepali doesn't change the adjective at all, it just uses **भन्दा** 'than': 'Kathmandu Pokhara-than big is'.

vocab.note: Also spelled रङ्ग. कस्तो रङ? 'what colour?'
Note the light nasal on the e (ँ).
Grey is also खरानी रङ 'ash colour'.
f बूढी; बूढा-बूढी 'old couple'. Polite: उमेर पुगेको.
Attached to what you compare with: मभन्दा 'than me'.

phrases.en: This is a bit too big.

phrases.native: सगरमाथा संसारको सबैभन्दा अग्लो हिमाल हो।
phrases.roman: Sagarmāthā sansārko sabaibhandā aglo himāl ho.
phrases.en: Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

grammar.title: Adjective agreement: -ओ, -आ, -ई
grammar.body:
Adjectives come **before** the noun. Only adjectives ending in **-ओ** change; the others (नयाँ, सफा, गुलाबी, शान्त…) never do.

**-ओ** — default: one male person, or any thing(s): ठूलो घर 'a big house'
**-आ** — plural people or respected persons: ठूला मान्छेहरू 'adults', मेरा बुबा
**-ई** — female persons: राम्री केटी 'a pretty girl', बूढी आमा

The same applies after the verb: केटी राम्री छ 'the girl is pretty'. In relaxed speech many people keep -ओ for plurals of things and even for people, but -ई with women and girls is still used by most speakers, and -आ is expected for respected men.

Note: 'too big' is usually expressed with भयो 'became': यो ठूलो भयो 'this is (turned out) too big'.

grammar.title: Comparing: भन्दा, सबैभन्दा, जत्तिकै
grammar.body:
**Comparative**: X **Y-भन्दा** [adjective] छ — 'X is more [adj] than Y'. The adjective itself doesn't change: पोखरा काठमाडौंभन्दा सानो छ 'Pokhara is smaller than Kathmandu'.

**Superlative**: **सबैभन्दा** + adjective — 'the most / -est': सबैभन्दा ठूलो 'the biggest'.

**Even more**: **अझ** — अझ राम्रो 'even better'. **A bit more**: अलि — अलि सानो 'a bit smaller'.

**As … as**: X **Y-जत्तिकै** [adj] छ: मेरो भाइ मजत्तिकै अग्लो छ 'my brother is as tall as me'. 'Not as … as': X Y-जत्तिको [adj] छैन.

examples.native: मेरी दिदी मभन्दा दुई वर्ष जेठी हुनुहुन्छ।
examples.roman: meri didi mabhandā dui barsa jeṭhi hunuhunchha.
examples.en: My sister is two years older than me.
Pokhara isn't as dirty as Kathmandu.

grammar.title: Intensifiers and doubling
grammar.body:
To strengthen or soften an adjective: **धेरै** 'very', **एकदम** 'really, totally', **निकै** 'quite, pretty', **अलि** 'a bit', **त्यति** (+ negative) 'not that', **कत्ति** (+ negative) 'not at all'.

**Doubling** an adjective gives a distributive or 'sort of / each one' meaning: साना-साना बच्चाहरू 'little little kids', रातो-रातो 'reddish / all red'. And **कति** + adjective makes an exclamation: कति राम्रो! 'how beautiful!'

examples.en: The food isn't spicy at all.

dialogue.title: Pokhara or Kathmandu?
dialogue.setting: Tom has just come back from a trip to Pokhara. His friend Anita asks him about it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: धेरै राम्रो! काठमाडौंभन्दा सानो छ, तर सफा छ।
lines.roman: dherai rāmro! Kāṭhmāḍauṃbhandā sāno chha, tara saphā chha.
lines.en: Really nice! It's smaller than Kathmandu, but clean.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: हो, पोखरा अलि शान्त पनि छ।
lines.roman: ho, Pokharā ali sānta pani chha.
lines.en: Yes, Pokhara is a bit quieter too.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: तर बेगनास ताल अझ शान्त छ।
lines.roman: tara Begnās Tāl ajha sānta chha.
lines.en: But Begnas Lake is even more peaceful.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: अनि माछापुच्छ्रे! सेतो, अग्लो — सबैभन्दा राम्रो हिमाल!
lines.roman: ani Māchhāpuchchhre! seto, aglo — sabaibhandā rāmro himāl!
lines.en: And Machhapuchhre! White, tall — the most beautiful mountain!

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: सबैभन्दा अग्लो चाहिँ सगरमाथा हो नि।
lines.roman: sabaibhandā aglo chāhiṃ Sagarmāthā ho ni.
lines.en: The highest one is Everest, though.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: थाहा छ, तर मलाई माछापुच्छ्रे नै सबैभन्दा राम्रो लाग्छ।
lines.roman: thāhā chha, tara malāi Māchhāpuchchhre nai sabaibhandā rāmro lāgchha.
lines.en: I know, but I think Machhapuchhre is the most beautiful.

lines.speaker: Anita
lines.native: तपाईंको ज्याकेट पनि नयाँ हो? रातो रङ राम्रो छ।
lines.roman: tapāiṃko jyākeṭ pani nayāṃ ho? rāto raṅ rāmro chha.
lines.en: Is your jacket new too? The red colour is nice.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: धन्यवाद! यो पोखराको हो — सस्तो पनि।
lines.roman: dhanyabād! yo Pokharāko ho — sasto pani.
lines.en: Thanks! It's from Pokhara — and cheap too.

culture: Colours carry meaning in Nepal: **red** (रातो) is the colour of weddings, married women's सिन्दूर (vermilion in the hair parting) and the red-green पोते bead necklace; **white** (सेतो) is worn in mourning. Personal remarks are frank and usually friendly: **मोटाउनुभएछ!** 'You've put on weight!' often means 'you look healthy and well-fed', while दुब्लाउनुभएछ 'you've got thin' is a sign of concern. Don't take either personally. Everest is **सगरमाथा** in Nepali and *Chomolungma* in Sherpa/Tibetan.

tip.title: Colours before the noun
tip.body:
- A colour (like any adjective) goes **before** the noun: **रातो** झोला 'a red bag'.
- Or after, with छ: झोला **रातो** छ 'the bag is red'.
- 'What colour?' = **कस्तो रङको**? or रङ कस्तो छ?

tip.title: Adjectives in -ओ change
tip.body:
- Adjectives ending in **-ओ** agree: **-ओ** for a man or any thing (ठूलो घर), **-ई** for a woman or girl (अग्ली बहिनी), **-आ** for a respected man or a plural (मेरा दाइ होचा हुनुहुन्छ).
- Other adjectives never change: जवान, नयाँ, सफा.
- The same goes after the verb: केटी **राम्री** छ.

lessons.title: Bigger, better, the best

tip.title: Comparing: -भन्दा and सबैभन्दा
tip.body:
- 'X is bigger than Y' = X **Y-भन्दा** ठूलो छ. The adjective doesn't change.
- 'The biggest' = **सबैभन्दा** ठूलो.
- **अझ** = 'even (more)': अझ राम्रो 'even better'.
- 'Not that…' = **त्यति** … छैन.
tip.pattern: X + Y-भन्दा + adjective + छ  ·  सबैभन्दा + adjective

lessons.title: Very, a bit, not at all

tip.title: Very, quite, a bit, not at all
tip.body:
- Before an adjective: **धेरै** / **एकदम** 'very, really', **निकै** 'quite', **अलि** 'a bit'.
- With a negative only: **त्यति** 'not that', **कत्ति** 'not at all': कत्ति पिरो छैन.
- **कति** + adjective = 'how …!': कति राम्रो!
- 'Too big' is often अलि ठूलो **भयो** 'turned out a bit big'.
tip.pattern: एकदम / निकै / अलि + adjective  ·  त्यति / कत्ति + adjective + छैन

sentences.en: The road is a bit long.
This bag is a bit too small.
The tea isn't sweet at all.
